title: How to Setup and Perform a qPCR Experiment
author: Promega
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.t8uerww

steps.title: Prepare DNA dilutions and samples
steps.instruction: Create the standard DNA dilution series and experimental samples in nuclease‑free water, then keep them on ice until use.

substeps.instruction: Prepare the standard DNA dilution series in nuclease‑free water.
Prepare experimental samples in nuclease‑free water.
Store all dilutions and samples on ice until use.

steps.title: Thaw and vortex master mix
steps.instruction: Thaw the GoTaq® qPCR Master Mix (Promega Cat #A6001) at room temperature, vortex gently without foaming or prolonged light exposure, and keep on ice.

substeps.instruction: Thaw GoTaq® qPCR Master Mix at room temperature.
Gently vortex to mix, avoiding foaming and extended exposure to light.
Store the master mix on ice until use.

steps.title: Prepare reaction mix without template
steps.instruction: Combine reagents in the order listed in Table 1 to make the reaction mix (no template), add any required reference or normalization dyes, and vortex gently avoiding foam.

substeps.instruction: Combine reagents according to Table 1 to create the reaction mix without template DNA.
If the instrument requires a CXR reference dye, add it as per the guidelines; for BioRad instruments add a normalization dye such as fluorescein.
Gently vortex the mix, taking care to avoid foaming.

steps.title: Add template or water to wells
steps.instruction: Dispense 10 μl of template DNA (or 10 μl water for no‑template controls) into the appropriate wells, then store the plate at room temperature or on ice.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 μl of template DNA to each designated well, or 10 μl water for NTC wells.
Store the reaction plate at room temperature or on ice.

steps.title: Add reaction mix to wells
steps.instruction: Add the calculated volume of reaction mix (e.g., 40 μl for a 50 μl total reaction) to each well, avoiding cross‑contamination.

substeps.instruction: Add the appropriate volume of the prepared reaction mix (e.g., 40 μl for a 50 μl reaction) to each well prepared in Step 1.

steps.title: Seal plate and centrifuge
steps.instruction: Seal the reaction plate and centrifuge at low speed for 1 minute to collect components and eliminate air bubbles.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at low speed for 1 minute to bring all components together and remove air bubbles.

steps.title: Program cycler and run qPCR
steps.instruction: Program the thermal cycler with the appropriate detection and reference dyes, select a standard or fast two‑step 40‑cycle program with dissociation, collect data during annealing, then start the run and analyze the results.

substeps.instruction: Program the thermal cycler per manufacturer instructions: select SYBR® or FAM™ as the detection dye for the whole plate; select the ROX™ channel for the CXR reference dye.
Choose a standard or fast two‑step qPCR program with 40 cycles and a dissociation step; set data collection during the annealing step of each cycle.
Place the sealed plate into the instrument and press “Start”.
When the run completes, analyze the data using standard procedures.
